verdict: Revenue was $729M — up 4% as reported and up 7% excluding the China diagnostics business being sold — with Life Sciences leading growth and management raising full-year guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +4% YoY as reported; +7% pro forma (excluding China IDX)

kpis.label: Full-year guidance
kpis.note: Pro forma revenue; pro forma adjusted EPS raised to $5.40–$5.45

segments.name: Life Sciences
segments.note: Tools and reagents that help researchers discover and develop new medicines

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.note: Tests for newborn screening, infectious disease and other conditions; the reported fall reflects the China business being sold — excluding it, growth was +4%

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new tests, instruments and software

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$18M is mainly $21M of interest expense, partly offset by interest income and a small investment gain, plus a $0.3M loss from discontinued operations. Figures are as reported (including the China diagnostics business being sold), not the pro forma view.

follow100Note: Whole-$M rounding: SG&A is shown as $276M (reported $275M) so the rounded figures balance exactly.

takeaways.title: Life Sciences led the quarter
takeaways.text: Life Sciences revenue rose to $380M, with pro forma organic growth of 9% (growth from the existing business, stripping out currency and deals).

takeaways.title: Diagnostics grew once the sale is stripped out
takeaways.text: Reported Diagnostics revenue fell 2% to $349M because it still includes the China immunodiagnostics business being divested. On a pro forma basis excluding it, Diagnostics grew 4%.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Revvity now expects pro forma adjusted EPS of $5.40–$5.45 for 2026 and pro forma revenue of about $2.86B with roughly 5% organic growth.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $28M in the quarter weighed on GAAP operating income of $95M; adjusted operating income was $209M.

Revvity has agreed to sell its China immunodiagnostics business (about 6% of 2025 revenue), expected to close by the end of 2027; results above are as reported, with pro forma figures excluding that business noted where relevant.
